material.witness: src/network/quic/connection.ts: mutable localMaxStreamsBidi and localMaxStreamsUni, a +1 credit when a peer stream closes both directions (RFC 9000 4.6 and 19.11), MAX_STREAMS queued as a max_streams record so loss retransmits it, STREAMS_BLOCKED as a safety valve, and the streams event unblocking the H3 client queue. material.commit_comment: HTTP/3 over QUIC v1 with a static-table QPACK, plus congestion control, pacing and loss recovery
material.subject: HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) over QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000, transport; RFC 9001, TLS 1.3 integration and packet protection) with QPACK (RFC 9204), client and server over the virtual UDP hub, including packet number spaces, header protection, ACK ranges, STREAM and CRYPTO frames, flow control, loss detection and PTO timers, connection IDs, idle timeout, and CONNECTION_CLOSE. Node 24.15 has no QUIC or HTTP/3 module (node:quic and node:http3 are unknown with and without --experimental-quic), so the references are: RFC 9001 Appendix A packet protection and initial-secret vectors, and aioquic 1.6.1 (installed in the scratch venv /tmp/owc-r4/quic-ref/venv) interop both directions through the bridge harness. Depends on owc-tls-functional (TLS 1.3 handshake in QUIC mode) and the UDP path of the bridge. Witness plan is staged: transport and packet protection vectors first, then handshake interop, then HTTP/3 request and response with QPACK static table, then streams and flow control under loss.
material.witness: src/network/quic: transport and packet protection, the TLS 1.3 handshake in QUIC mode, connection.ts, recovery.ts, h3-connection.ts, h3-api.ts and the QPACK codec. An independent adversarial verifier, re-run here, reports zero failures on all three previously open claims: 300 of 300 and 1000 of 1000 sequential requests with MAX_STREAMS growing on the wire and no credit leak; the peer observing the client's CONNECTION_CLOSE code 256 at five of five call sites including under 10 percent loss; and NewReno with pacing where a 2.5 second blackout yields ssthresh 2400 equal to the minimum window, the signature of RFC 9002 7.6.2, recovering afterwards and never collapsing. Eleven loss and reordering runs of 1 MiB each delivered byte-exact data across 0, 1, 5, 10 and 20 percent loss in each direction and 10 and 30 percent reordering. Handshake at 10 and 20 percent loss, key update with and without loss, idle timeout, a malformed frame giving 261 and header blocks up to 1.1 MB giving 263 all behave correctly. Not implemented and explicitly out of scope: 0-RTT, migration, ECN and stateless reset. Throughput of 70 to 260 KB/s is attributed to the send loop and bridge rather than congestion control and stays open as owc-guest-transport-throughput.

No postinstall step leaves the tree in a half-installed state

material.description: The corpus entry esbuild-native reports HOST_INSTALL: esbuild's npm postinstall runs the platform binary it shipped, which is a real executable and cannot run in the container. Either install the package without running that step (esbuild ships a js-install / ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH path) or make the install refuse with one clear line naming the binary, instead of failing inside a postinstall script the user never sees.
material.resolution: Refusal branch taken: esbuild ships no JavaScript or WebAssembly fallback, so it cannot work in a JavaScript-only container. packages/core/src/npm/native.ts finds the executable a package's platform dependency shipped (ELF/Mach-O/PE, skipping .node/.so/.dylib/.dll, which are loaded not executed), and packages/core/src/npm/installer.ts refuses the install script with ENOEXEC naming it, before the script runs. Live run: npm install esbuild exits 126 with 'npm error esbuild@0.24.2 runs the native executable /work/node_modules/@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild in its postinstall script; this container executes JavaScript only'; require('esbuild').transformSync still fails afterwards, as expected. Previous behaviour was a QuickJS abort (RuntimeError: null function or function signature mismatch) naming only 'node install.js'. core-js regression: install exit 0, postinstall runs, works.
